Augusta GA Outdoor Activities: The Definitive Local Guide

When people think of Augusta, Georgia, they think of one thing: golf. And yes, Augusta National Golf Club is a bucket-list destination. But limiting Augusta to its most famous 18 holes is like calling Savannah a college town — technically true, wildly incomplete. The real Augusta is a city wrapped around the Savannah River, with 40+ miles of paved trails, a whitewater canal, public kayak launches, and a downtown riverfront that locals actually use. Whether you're planning a weekend visit or you live here and need a Saturday plan, this guide covers the Augusta GA outdoor activities worth your time — and the one place to stay that puts you directly on the water.

1. Walk the Augusta Riverwalk and Riverfront

The Augusta Riverwalk is the city's outdoor living room. This paved, multi-level promenade runs along the Savannah River from the 5th Street Bridge to the 8th Street Plaza, with overlooks, amphitheater steps, and benches that face the water. Start at the Augusta Convention & Visitors Bureau on Broad Street, grab a coffee, and walk the full loop — it's about a mile and a half round trip and flat enough for strollers and bikes.

What locals know

  • Best time: Early morning (before 8 a.m.) for calm water and empty paths, or sunset for the river reflecting the bridge lights.
  • Don't miss: The Augusta Museum of History sits right off the Riverwalk if you want a quick indoor break.
  • Parking: Use the free lot at the 8th Street Plaza — downtown meters are enforced on weekdays.

2. Kayak or Paddleboard the Savannah River

The Savannah River is Augusta's biggest outdoor asset, and the best way to experience it is from the water. Several local outfitters rent kayaks and paddleboards by the hour, but the smartest move — especially for groups — is to stay somewhere with kayaks included. That's where KJ Augusta Rentals' Entire River House comes in: the property includes six kayaks, a private dock, and a boat slip directly on the river. You launch from the backyard, not a crowded public ramp.

If you're paddling on your own, put in at the Augusta Canal headgates or the 5th Street launch. The current is gentle upstream of the city, making it beginner-friendly. Watch for the occasional barge — give them plenty of room.

3. Bike or Hike the Augusta Canal Trail

The Augusta Canal National Heritage Area is one of the most underrated outdoor activities in Georgia. The towpath trail runs roughly 7 miles from the headgates at 13th Street to the Savannah Rapids Pavilion, and it's flat, shaded, and crushed-gravel — perfect for hybrid bikes, trail runners, and families. Rent a bike from a downtown shop or bring your own; the trail connects to the Riverwalk via a short connector near 5th Street.

Trail highlights

  • Savannah Rapids Pavilion: A scenic overlook and picnic area at the northern end.
  • Lake Olmstead: A calm reservoir perfect for a mid-ride break.
  • Wildlife: Herons, turtles, and the occasional alligator — keep your distance.

4. Explore Phinizy Swamp Nature Park

Phinizy Swamp Nature Park is 1,100 acres of wetlands, boardwalks, and birding trails about 10 minutes south of downtown. It's free, open daily from dawn to dusk, and genuinely one of the best outdoor activities in Augusta for families and photographers. The boardwalk loop is stroller-friendly; the longer dike trails are gravel and better for hiking boots.

Bring bug spray in summer and binoculars year-round — Phinizy is a known stopover for migratory birds.

5. Play Disc Golf at Pendleton King Park

Pendleton King Park on Troupe Street is a local favorite for a reason: it has a well-maintained 18-hole disc golf course, a dog park, and walking trails through old-growth pines. Discs are cheap, the course is free, and it's a genuinely fun Augusta GA fun activity that doesn't require a tee time. Combine it with a stop at the nearby Augusta Market (Saturdays, 8 a.m.–2 p.m. at the 8th Street Plaza) for local produce and food trucks.

6. Catch a GreenJackets Game at SRP Park

Baseball is an outdoor activity, and SRP Park in North Augusta — just across the river from downtown — is one of the nicest minor-league ballparks in the Southeast. The Augusta GreenJackets (Single-A affiliate of the Atlanta Braves) play from April through September. Tickets are affordable, the river views from the concourse are excellent, and the atmosphere is family-friendly. Pair it with a Riverwalk stroll before first pitch.

7. Golf (Obviously) — But Skip the Crowds

You can't write about Augusta outdoor activities without mentioning golf, but here's the local secret: you don't need a Masters badge to play great golf in Augusta. Public courses like Forest Hills Golf Club (where Ben Hogan once played) and the J. Perry Golf Course at the Augusta Municipal Golf Course offer affordable tee times year-round. During Masters Week, tee times are scarce and prices spike — which is exactly why staying outside downtown matters. KJ Augusta Rentals is 15 minutes from Augusta National via a private back route that avoids the worst of the Washington Road traffic. If you're coming for the tournament, that alone is worth the booking.

8. Fish the Savannah River and Local Lakes

The Savannah River holds striped bass, largemouth bass, and catfish. Public access points include the boat ramp at the 5th Street Bridge and the Savannah Rapids Pavilion. If you're staying at KJ's river house, you have a private dock and boat slip — bring your rod and fish from the dock at dawn, or launch a boat without fighting a public ramp.

Where to Stay in Augusta for Outdoor Access

Here's the thing most visitors don't realize until they've already booked: downtown Augusta hotels are fine for a convention, but they're a terrible base for an outdoor-focused trip. You'll pay for parking (often $20–$30/night downtown, and significantly more during Masters Week), deal with traffic on Broad Street, and drive 20+ minutes to reach any actual trailhead or river access. Generic short-term rentals aren't much better — many are shared properties with other guests on-site, thin walls, and no outdoor space beyond a small balcony.

KJ Augusta Rentals is the clear alternative. The property sits on 3 private acres directly on the Savannah River, with a saltwater pool overlooking the water, six included kayaks, a private dock and boat slip, a fire pit, propane and charcoal grills, ping pong, cornhole, and a golf tee-off area. It sleeps up to 16 across 4 bedrooms — and critically, there are no shared guests or other parties on site. You book the entire property or a private portion of it, and you pay the owner directly, which means no Airbnb or VRBO platform fees tacked onto your total.

Three stay options fit different groups:

  • Entire River House — sleeps up to 16, ideal for family reunions, golf groups, or corporate retreats.
  • Upstairs River House — a smaller footprint for groups of 6–10 who still want full river access.
  • River Suite — a couples' option with the same waterfront setting and pool access.

Compared to a downtown hotel room with a parking garage view, the difference isn't subtle. You wake up on the river, kayak before breakfast, and drive 15 minutes to Augusta National via the back route when it's tournament week. Check availability and book direct at kjaugustarentals.com — no platform fees, you pay the owner directly.

Plan Your Augusta Outdoor Weekend

The best Augusta GA outdoor activities aren't hidden — they're just overlooked by visitors who never leave the golf course bubble. Walk the Riverwalk at sunrise, paddle the Savannah, bike the canal towpath, and end the day by a fire pit on the water. That's a weekend that beats a hotel stay every time. And if you want the outdoor access built into your accommodations, KJ's river house is the only place in Augusta that gives you 3 private acres, a saltwater pool, and six kayaks without sharing a single square foot with strangers.
